displayDescription: A clay idea bulb lands on a dark slate studio sweep. Clay tubes extrude from it and connect to falling orbs, forming a settled network.
styleRenderer: Three.js WebGLRenderer (procedural rounded meshes, matte MeshStandardMaterial with seeded bump grain, PCF soft shadows, blob contact shadows, NeutralToneMapping)
motionEngine: GSAP paused timeline (single scene-time owner + copy reveals)
Analytic keyed squash/stretch functions of time
Extended Position-Based Dynamics (XPBD) rope bake, fixed 24 substeps per frame, cached at load
audioDescription: Silent preview. No audio track, music, effects or voice.
limitations: Reviewed renderer Blender/bpy/Cycles could not run: Blender 5.2.2 segfaults at startup inside this sandbox while detecting the Metal GPU backend (before any Python executes). The scene was instead built with Three.js (STYLE.json-listed alternative) in WebGL; this is rasterized lighting with shadow maps, not path tracing, so there is no true global illumination, subsurface scattering or ray-traced ambient occlusion — contact shadows are approximated with blob textures.
Clay-like digital treatment only; no physical clay or stop motion was filmed. Surface grain is seeded procedural value noise used as a bump map.
Squash/stretch is an analytic damped-cosine scale on rigid meshes (volume-preserving approximation), not soft-body deformation.
Tube sag uses a simplified XPBD chain (distance + soft bending constraints, gravity, floor contact with approximate friction); it is illustrative, not validated physics.

Optional preview recipe list was empty; the refresh demonstrates the reviewed source-frame lesson: a scene-dependent dark stage with radial falloff, a value-contrasted matte hero, a single complementary accent family, and flat 2D type layered over the 3D scene.
Three.js internals contain Math.random for object UUIDs only; no visual state depends on it.
